newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares down, seek fuel for new advance.
newsitem.headline: German shares down, seek fuel for new advance.

text.p: German shares were down in early listless trade on Thursday as traders said the market searched for fuel for a new advance on record levels.
The DAX index was down 20.00 points at 3,568.57 points in pre-bourse IBIS computer dealings, down from the DAX index's close in bourse trade on Wednesday at 3,573.69 points.

Traders said options expiries on the DAX index and on shares would likely keep the market under pressure. Another factor was next Tuesday's FOMC meeting and the ongoing debate whether the Federal Reserve will raise U.S. interest rates.

"There's not much room for movement right now and it looks as though we are going to be locked in somewhat volatile range trade," said one Frankfurt dealer who looked for a DAX trading range from 3,565 to 3,595 points for the coming sessions.
Carmakers, hurt by the weaker dollar, were down along with the market despite the VDA German automobile association reporting a 15 percent year-on-year rise in vehicle production.
Volkswagen AG was down 6.25 marks at 1,151.75, Daimler-Benz AG was down 50 pfennigs at 134 marks and BMW AG fell two marks to 1,462 marks.

The BMW losses came despite the carmaker reporting a provisional 17.4 percent rise in five-month sales to 24.3 billion marks and a nearly eight percent rise in vehicle deliveries to 497,000 for the period from January to May.

Chemical shares were also lower with the market and also due to the dollar despite BASF AG saying its 1997 sales would top 50 billion marks and that sales and profits would remain at high levels in the coming months.
BASF shares fell 1.20 marks to 66.50 marks, while rivals Hoechst AG was down 38 pfennigs at 65.28 marks and Bayer AG slipped 10 pfennigs to 65.56 marks.
